question: What is the primary structural change that happens inside a joint affected by osteoarthritis?

options.A: Rapid overgrowth of synovial fluid in the joint
options.B: Destruction and breakdown of articular cartilage
options.C: Infection of the bone marrow by bacteria
options.D: Calcification of the surrounding muscle fibers

explanation: Osteoarthritis primarily targets the smooth articular cartilage that protects the ends of bones within a joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: Osteophytes develop in osteoarthritis primarily as a result of what process?

options.A: Bacterial invasion of the joint capsule during injury
options.B: Scar tissue replacement of torn muscle ligaments
options.C: Excessive calcium deposits from dietary supplements
options.D: Bone remodeling and friction from bone-on-bone contact

explanation: Bone spurs or osteophytes form as the body attempts to repair the damaged joint and distribute increased mechanical stress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which factor is considered a primary non-modifiable risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?
explanation: Aging cannot be modified and represents the single greatest risk factor due to cumulative joint use over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: Obesity accelerates the progression of osteoarthritis in weight-bearing joints by causing what effect?

options.A: Increasing mechanical stress and joint loading
options.C: Decreasing systemic blood flow to the cartilage

explanation: Extra body mass multiplies the compressive forces acting on weight-bearing surfaces such as the knees and hips daily. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: What is the typical duration of morning stiffness experienced by a patient with osteoarthritis?
explanation: Morning stiffness in osteoarthritis is brief, typically resolving in under half an hour of waking up. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: A patient describes joint pain that follows a specific daily pattern. What pattern is most characteristic of osteoarthritis?

options.A: Pain is most severe in the morning and disappears at noon
options.B: Pain worsens with physical activity and improves with rest
options.C: Pain remains constant and never changes with movement
options.D: Pain occurs only when the patient is completely resting

explanation: Mechanical wear causes pain to increase when using the joint, while resting provides temporary relief. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which diagnostic imaging tool is most commonly used to confirm the presence of osteoarthritis?
explanation: Simple X-rays clearly display the characteristic bone changes and joint space narrowing associated with osteoarthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why do doctors order blood tests like the erythrocyte sedimentation rate when evaluating a patient with joint pain?

options.A: To calculate the patient's risk of future bone fractures
options.B: To rule out systemic inflammatory and autoimmune diseases
options.C: To detect bacterial growth inside the synovial fluid
options.D: To measure the exact amount of remaining joint cartilage

explanation: Normal inflammatory blood markers help differentiate mechanical osteoarthritis from systemic inflammatory conditions like rheumatoid arthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: Which medication is frequently prescribed as a first-line oral analgesic for mild osteoarthritis pain?
explanation: Acetaminophen is commonly chosen first due to its favorable safety profile for mild joint discomfort. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: What is a major clinical consideration when administering nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs to older adults over a long period?

options.A: Risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and renal impairment
options.B: Permanent darkening of the skin over the joints
options.C: Development of severe physical addiction and dependence
options.D: Sudden spikes in resting blood glucose levels

explanation: Long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can compromise the gastric mucosa and reduce renal blood flow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which type of physical activity is most appropriate for a client diagnosed with osteoarthritis?
explanation: Low-impact activities strengthen supporting muscles without subjecting the damaged joint to excessive shock. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: A nurse recommends the use of a walking cane to a patient with knee osteoarthritis. What is the primary purpose of this intervention?

options.A: To improve cardiovascular endurance during walks
options.B: To decrease load bearing on the affected joint
options.C: To stimulate rapid production of new cartilage
options.D: To prevent the patient from falling asleep

explanation: Using an assistive device in the hand opposite the affected limb helps transfer body weight away from the painful joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is the definitive surgical procedure performed for severe, end-stage osteoarthritis of the hip or knee?
explanation: Joint replacement removes the ruined articular surfaces entirely and substitutes them with durable artificial implants. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h7)

question: Why might a surgeon perform an osteotomy instead of an immediate joint replacement in a younger patient?

options.A: To permanently cure the systemic inflammatory process
options.B: To shift mechanical weight away from the damaged area
options.C: To remove all loose bone fragments from the capsule
options.D: To eliminate the need for any postoperative therapy

explanation: An osteotomy cuts and reshapes bone to transfer stress to a healthier part of the joint, delaying replacement surgery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h7)

question: Which complication is a major safety concern for elderly clients suffering from advanced osteoarthritis in the lower extremities?
explanation: Joint pain, stiffness, and instability significantly impair balance and increase the likelihood of falling. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: What is a vital component of home management education for a patient newly diagnosed with osteoarthritis?

options.A: Injecting prescribed corticosteroids into the joint independently
options.B: Learning proper body mechanics and weight control strategies
options.C: Avoiding all forms of physical movement to protect cartilage
options.D: Stopping all medications once the daily pain subsides

explanation: Long-term self-management requires lifestyle changes like protecting joints and reducing weight to slow disease progression. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)
